messages:
mara: Heads-up — we've got a handful of customer escalations (two enterprise customers + support thread) about p95/p99 spikes on text-generation endpoints. Started ~1h ago. Sample request_id=cr-7f8a2. Symptoms: p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~700-900ms for small-ish requests. Correlated metric I see is prefix_kv_cache miss_rate spiking to ~0.8.

eli: @mara thanks. I already pulled cache stats for the region shard that serves those customers. Short dump: cache_entries=128k, cache_size_bytes=9.8GB, evictions/sec=1.2k, prefix_kv_miss_rate=0.82, prefix_kv_hit_rate=0.18. Also saw huge variance in request latency tail.

sanjay: Any recent infra/runtime changes?

mara: We shipped a change last night (PR #7123) that swapped the eviction policy to "clock_pro" and changed cache key assembly for prefixes (intended to dedupe redundant prefixes). Could be related.

eli: Poked logs. Repro snippet from inference node logs:
```
[INFO] 2026-03-14T21:05:12Z cache_miss prefix=/customers/acme/stack/ model=gpt-medium key=/customers/acme/stack//gpt-medium:user123
[DEBUG] 2026-03-14T21:05:12Z build_key prefix=/customers/acme/stack/ model=gpt-medium user=user123 -> /customers/acme/stack//gpt-medium:user123
[WARN] 2026-03-14T21:05:12Z cache_evict victim_key=/customers/acme/stack/old:gpt-medium
```

eli: Notice the double-slash in key creation. Looks like key normalization bug: sometimes prefix has trailing slash, sometimes not -> different cache keys for same logical prefix. That will blow up effective cache utilization and cause thrash with the new eviction policy.

mara: repro steps I used: 1) Run a small script hitting /v1/generate with prefix "/customers/acme/stack/" then again with "/customers/acme/stack"; 2) Observe cache stats via /metrics endpoint; 3) Notice miss_rate goes way up when requests vary. I attached the minimal repro script below.
```
# repro.sh
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gpt-medium","prompt":"hi","prefix":"/customers/acme/stack/"}' >/dev/null
  sleep 0.01
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gpt-medium","prompt":"hi","prefix":"/customers/acme/stack"}' >/dev/null
done
```

laura: That explains the thrash. Two different keys for same logical cache entry + clock_pro accelerates evictions for entries not recently referenced — leads to p99 tail.

eli: Short-term mitigations we applied: 
- rolled back PR #7123 (eviction policy change) on the affected pool (command: `infractl rollback pool=us-west-2/shard-9 --pr=7123`)
- enabled prefix normalization on the request path as a defensive toggle: `runtime.config.prefix_kv.normalize=true` (hotpatch)
- temporarily increased prefix_kv_cache.size_bytes from 10GB -> 16GB for the hot shards to reduce eviction pressure
After those, observed p95 for the customer sample drop from ~720ms to ~210ms within ~5m. Miss rate went from 0.82 -> 0.23.

mara: Great. Did we confirm the normalization fix is safe for other customers? Any semantic risk of collapsing distinct prefixes?

eli: We validated on a staging tenant set. Normalization only strips duplicate trailing slashes and collapses consecutive slashes; it does NOT fold different path segments. Example: "/a/b" and "/a/b/" become "/a/b". I ran a few test suites and the model routing logic didn't break.

sanjay: For the long-term: we need to harden key construction and add stronger invariants. Proposed items:
- Fix code to always normalize prefix at ingress and at cache key writer (two layers)
- Add unit tests and fuzzing for prefix edge cases (leading/trailing slashes, URL-encoded chars)
- Re-evaluate eviction policy; clock_pro might be fine but needs hit-rate costing model per workload
- Add a metric `prefix_kv_effective_utilization` = logical_prefix_groups / physical_entries to detect this class of problems early

laura: I'll create a task in runtime backlog: RUNTIME-1187 "Cache key normalization + tests" and link to this thread. Also RUNTIME-1188 for eviction policy analysis.

ops-bot: Created incident INC-4321; severity: P2; assignees: eli, laura; pager duty notified.

mara: Support update I posted to customer: "We've identified cache key normalization and eviction interactions as root cause; mitigation applied (hotpatch + rollback). We'll follow up with timeline and long-term fix. Apologized and offered credits." Support logged two escalations: SR-9284 & SR-9287.

eli: Follow-ups I'm doing today:
- open PR to add normalization at the serializer + add unit tests (target: rollout in 24h)
- create dashboards/alerts: warn if prefix_kv_miss_rate > 0.3 for >5m or evictions/sec > 500 for >2m
- run controlled canary of clock_pro with synthetic load that varies prefix formats to measure sensitivity

mara: Any other immediate mitigation suggestions? Could we add a short-term request-side dedupe (normalize prefix before enqueuing) as a quick band-aid?

eli: Already enabled normalization toggle; it's request-side and runtime-level. We should be good for now. Also scheduled a cluster-wide cache warmup for top 200 prefixes for enterprise tenants (script run at 22:30 UTC).

sanjay: When we re-enable new eviction policy we should run a canary with strict telemetry: effective_utilization, miss_rate, p95/p99, evictions/sec, and fallback_count. If any one metric regresses beyond threshold auto-rollback.

laura: I'll own the post-incident writeup. Action items: RUNTIME-1187, RUNTIME-1188, setup alerts (dashboards ticket), add synthetic canary job. ETA for full fix (tests + rollout + docs): 1 week.

mara: Thanks all. Please make sure support closes SRs after we confirm customer latency returns to normal for 24h. Leave thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
